battle.name: 齊魏戰爭
battle.brief: 479年十一月，蕭道成代宋建齊的同年冬，北魏孝文帝拓跋宏以劉昶為號召，三路南下：元嘉出淮陰、拓跋琛出廣陵、薛虎子出壽春。齊以垣崇祖守壽春、崔文仲當鍾離、蕭景先備義陽，節節抵住魏軍。卡面秦連弩正落在城頭：壽春小城、角城、朐山的強弩壓住攻城者，與壽春決堰的水功同樣替南齊守住淮泗。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 交戰的兩方是北魏與南齊。北魏是拓跋鮮卑建立的北方政權，都城平城，疆域北抵陰山、南跨淮北，漢地郡縣與鮮卑八部軍鎮並行，調兵沿用「假王」「公」為一軍之主的舊例，各領若干將軍與兵眾，並以行台、都督分道督軍；479年南征的三路就是這樣編成的：假梁郡王元嘉督二將出淮陰，隴西公拓跋琛三將出廣陵，河東公薛虎子三將出壽春，另有車騎大將軍昌黎王馮熙以西道都督出義陽。軍隊骨幹是騎兵與甲騎，步兵列於兩翼，攻城另配雲梯、撞車之屬，糧秣靠車隊自平城、洛陽分批運到前線。南齊是蕭道成於479年四月代劉宋而建的王朝，都建康，中樞設中軍將軍宿衛石頭城，地方則以州刺史、郡太守、鎮戍主逐層防守，兵源分禁軍、州郡兵、鎮兵與水軍。本役齊方統兵者分屬豫州（垣崇祖）、司州（蕭景先）、荊州（蕭嶷）、徐州（崔文仲）、兗州（周山圖）諸州，另有建康派出的援軍與海上運輸線。魏齊在淮水南北各據要衝：壽春、鍾離、下蔡在淮南，廣陵、淮陰、朐山、角城、泗口在淮北，夾水而峙，誰守住渡口與城垣，誰就守住這一線。
countriesEn: The two sides in this war were Northern Wei and Southern Qi. Northern Wei was the northern state founded by the Tuoba Xianbei, with its capital at Pingcheng, its territory reaching from the Yinshan range in the north down to the land north of the Huai in the south, and it governed Han commanderies and counties alongside the tribal garrisons of the eight Xianbei divisions. Troops were raised under an old convention in which a prince by investiture or a duke acted as the head of an army with several generals and their men beneath him, while executive offices and commandants supervised separate lines of advance; the three columns that marched south in 479 were organised in precisely that fashion: the Liang Commandery Prince by Investiture Yuan Jia with two generals through Huaiyin, the Duke of Longxi Tuoba Chen with three generals through Guangling, and the Duke of Hedong Xue Huzi with three generals through Shouchun, while the General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Changli, Feng Xi, moved out through Yiyang as commander of the western line. The backbone of the Wei army was cavalry and armoured horse, with infantry on the wings, siege equipment such as scaling ladders and battering rams for work against the walls, and grain and provisions brought to the front in wagon convoys from Pingcheng and Luoyang. Southern Qi was the dynasty that Xiao Daocheng founded in the fourth month of 479 by taking the throne from the Liu Song, with its capital at Jiankang. At the centre it kept a General of the Central Army quartered at Shitou, while locally defence ran down through provincial governors, commandery administrators and garrison commanders, and the manpower came from the imperial guard, provincial and commandery levies, garrison troops and riverine units. In this campaign the Qi commanders came from several provinces: Yu, commanded by Yuan Chongzu, Si, by Xiao Jingxian, Jing, by Xiao Yi, Xu, by Cui Wenzhong and Yan, by Zhou Shantu, in addition to reinforcements dispatched from Jiankang and a sea-borne supply route. Wei and Qi stood facing each other across the Huai: Shouchun, Zhongli and Xiacai lay south of the water, while Guangling, Huaiyin, Qiushan, Jiaocheng and Sikou lay north of it. Whoever held the fords and the walls held the line.
people: 北魏方面，名義上的統帥是年僅十二歲的孝文帝拓跋宏，但詔令以他名義發出，朝政由攝政的廣平王拓跋丕與李衝等人主持，這次出兵即由魏廷議定後分道發動。真正到前線指揮的是一批宗室與漢化派將領：假梁郡王元嘉即郁豆眷，督兩將出淮陰；隴西公拓跋琛出廣陵；河東公薛虎子出壽春；昌黎王馮熙以車騎大將軍督眾退軍、隨後又任西道都督出義陽；淮陽王尉元奉命平五固義眾；平南將軍郎大檀出朐城；鎮南將軍賀羅出下蔡；將軍白吐頭、元泰、封延各當一路；樂陵鎮將韋珍在義陽接應內附者。降魏多年的前宋宗室義陽王劉昶隨軍而行，北魏以「奉劉昶恢復宋室」為出兵名號；大陽蠻帥桓誕自請為前鋒，受授南征西道大都督。齊方與北魏接戰最烈的是豫州刺史垣崇祖，他早看準北魏必以壽春為突破口；司州刺史蕭景先在義陽、平昌一線嚴備；荊州刺史豫章王蕭嶷遣中兵參軍蕭惠朗領二千人、劉伾緒領千人分路應敵；徐州刺史崔文仲在鍾離破敵，又派軍主崔孝伯渡淮追擊，朐山戍主玄元度嬰城固守，海路上的崔靈建連夜趕到，以火炬虛張聲勢迫退魏軍。齊高帝蕭道成本人未赴前線，卻在出戰前對垣崇祖說破北魏必以劉昶為辭、必衝壽春，又遣驍騎將軍王洪範出使柔然約期夾擊，遺憾柔然騎兵只抵平城七百里便獵還而回，齊軍未及出師。
peopleEn: On the Wei side the nominal commander in chief was Emperor Xiaowen, Tuoba Hong, who was only twelve years old; the edicts nonetheless went out in his name, and the business of state was conducted by the regency headed by Prince of Guangping Tuoba Pi together with men such as Li Chong, the decision to invade being settled in the Wei court and then dispatched along separate lines. Those who actually led troops in the field were a mixture of imperial clan members and sinicising commanders: the Liang Commandery Prince by Investiture Yuan Jia, also known as Yudoujuan, with two generals through Huaiyin; the Duke of Longxi Tuoba Chen through Guangling; the Duke of Hedong Xue Huzi through Shouchun; the General of Chariots and Cavalry and later commander of the western line, Prince of Changli, Feng Xi, first receiving the withdrawing armies and then marching out through Yiyang; the Prince of Huaiyang Wei Yuan, sent to suppress the insurgents at Wugu; the General of Pacification of the South Lang Datan through Qiushan; the General of Garrisoning the South Helao through Xiacai; and the generals Bai Tutou, Yuan Tai and Feng Yan, each covering a route of his own, with the commander of Leling, Wei Zhen, going to the support of those who came over in Yiyang. Liu Chang, the former Prince of Yiyang of the Liu Song, who had fled north years earlier and was treated with marked favour by the Wei court, marched with the army, for Northern Wei fought under the banner of restoring the Song house to him. Huan Dan, the tribal chief of the Great Yang Man, volunteered for the vanguard and was appointed commander of the western route for the southern expedition. On the Qi side the sharpest fighting came at Shouchun against the Yu Province governor Yuan Chongzu, who had read the Wei plan correctly beforehand; the Si Province governor Xiao Jingxian held Yiyang and Pingchang in readiness; the Jing Province governor, Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Yi, sent the Colonel of Central Army Xiao Huilang with two thousand men and Liu Pixu with a thousand along separate roads to meet the enemy; the Xu Province governor Cui Wenzhong broke the Wei attack at Zhongli and then sent the unit commander Cui Xiaobo across the river in pursuit, while the garrison commander of Qiushan, Xuan Yuandu, held his city and the sea-borne reinforcement under Cui Lingjian came up in the night and put the enemy off with torches. The Qi emperor Xiao Daocheng himself did not take the field, but before the campaign he told Yuan Chongzu plainly that the barbarians did not understand the turn of fortune and would certainly move their masses to send Liu Chang forward, and that the thrust would come at Shouchun; he also sent the General of Valiant Cavalry Wang Hongfan to the Rouran to arrange a pincer attack. The Rouran horsemen got within seven hundred li of Pingcheng and then turned back after hunting, and the Qi army never marched out to meet them.
kits: 卡面那件秦連弩是弩機儲力、一踩一發的連發弩，這種形制在秦代已用於守城，《墨子》備穴一類的守城論述已把可連發的弩列為壓制攻城的常備。本役裡它落的位置很明確：壽春小城、角城、朐山的城頭。攻城方北魏的常規打法是「肉薄」——士卒披甲持盾、扛雲梯、推撞車密集貼到壕溝與城根，攀梯而上；守方的強弩手在城頭逐段射擊，弩機蓄力、上弦、發射一氣呵成，連發弩可以在梯密人稠的瞬間以高射速把攀梯的隊形壓回牆下，卡面那件兵器代表的正是這種守城一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外的用法。壽春之戰把這點講到最透：魏軍集中兵力攻堰北小城，城頭的弩把攻城隊形釘在濠外，垣崇祖看準時機決堤放水，洪水自狹窄水道奔下，攻城之眾連人馬漂墜溝塹，溺死數千人，弩火與水攻前後銜接，一守一放，決定了整場戰役。其餘諸城，朐山靠守軍嬰城、援軍夜以火炬虛張聲勢而退敵，角城守軍苦戰到成買戰死，鍾離則由崔文仲在城下反擊破敵。魏軍一方的攻城器械與騎兵，史料只作「逼攻」「肉薄」的簡筆，未細列名目，按當時通例則是雲梯、撞車、楯車、塹壕與穴地並行；魏軍另有大量騎兵在兩翼搜掠與截斷糧道。齊軍還靠水軍沿淮泗轉運，垣崇祖修堰用的是城西北的肥水，堰本身既是武器也是工事。
kitsEn: The piece on the card, the Qin repeating crossbow, is a weapon whose trigger mechanism stores the pull of the bow so that the bow can be loosed again with a single step of the foot; that form already served in defence under the Qin, and the siege writings of the Mohist school, in the chapter on preparing for sapping and tunnelling, list the repeating crossbow among the standard arms for holding attackers down. In this campaign its place is quite clear: on the walls of the small city at Shouchun, of Jiaocheng and of Qiushan. The standard method of Northern Wei in assaulting a wall was to go in thick: armoured soldiers with shields, carrying scaling ladders and pushing battering rams, crowded up to the ditch and the foot of the wall to climb; the defending crossbowmen on the wall answered in sections, the mechanism storing the draw, the string being set and the bolt loosed in one motion, and a repeating crossbow could, in the crowded moment when ladders and men were thickest below, put a high rate of fire down and push the climbing formation back from the wall. The card weapon stands for exactly that use: the defenders rely on it to hold the men who are attacking outside the wall. The battle of Shouchun makes the point most sharply of all. Wei concentrated its strength against the small city north of the dam, the crossbows on the wall pinned the assaulting formation outside the ditch, and Yuan Chongzu, judging the moment, cut the dam and let the water down; the flood rushed through the narrow channel, men and horses were swept into the ditch and drowned by the thousand, and the crossbow fire and the water came one after the other, one holding and one releasing, and settled the whole campaign. In the other cities Qiushan was saved by the garrison holding its walls and by a relief force that came up at night and raised torches to bluff the enemy off, Jiaocheng was fought to the death until its commander Cheng Mai fell, and at Zhongli the Qi turned the assault round under Cui Wenzhong. The Wei siege equipment and cavalry are only sketched in the sources, which say that the walls were pressed and that the men went in thick without naming the machines, but by the general practice of the time scaling ladders, battering and shielded rams, ditches and sapping were all employed together. Wei also put a great many horsemen on the flanks to forage and to cut the supply road. The Qi used riverine units to shift stores along the Huai and the Si, and the water that Yuan Chongzu dammed was the Fei, which runs past the north-west corner of the city; the dam was at once a weapon and a work of fortification.
tactics: 北魏的打法是多路並進加聲東擊西：淮陰、廣陵、壽春三處同時發兵，廣陵方向先動，南兗州刺史王敬則聽到魏軍越淮便棄鎮奔建康，齊廷一度把重兵壓在建康與石頭城，淮南一線因此吃緊；魏人同時用招撫做內應，義陽有人自稱司州刺史、角城戍主舉城降、汝南太守與龍驤將軍率眾內屬，內外一齊動手。攻城時魏軍把主力壓在壽春堰北小城，企圖破堰而後自東道進逼，垣崇祖卻故意不守外城，改為築堰立小城、深塹環之，斷言虜貪而少慮必悉力攻小城圖破此堰，待攻城者蟻附而聚，遂決小史埭放水淹營，魏軍全敗。守方的另一套辦法是死守與反擊：朐山玄元度嬰城固守，援軍崔靈建以火炬虛張，角城成買血戰至死，鍾離由崔文仲反敗為勝並遣崔孝伯渡淮追擊。李安民在淮陽打的是最漂亮的一仗：先派族弟長文領二百騎為前驅且退且戰，把數千魏騎引入林地，主力自伏兵處趨出，合戰於孫溪渚、戰父彎側，魏軍大敗，赴清水死不可勝數；二月遊擊將軍桓康再於淮陽破敵，攻陷樊諧城，垣崇祖亦趁魏軍毀下蔡戍之機渡河北擊。外交與游擊同為戰法一部分：出使柔然以牽制平城，魏軍則派尉元、薛虎子掃平五固義眾，切斷齊方內應；撤退時魏廷詔馮熙督眾接應，諸軍徐徐而退，未至崩潰。
tacticsEn: Northern Wei fought with several columns moving at once and with a feint on one front: the thrusts through Huaiyin, Guangling and Shouchun began together, and the column through Guangling moved first, so that Wang Jingzhe, governor of Southern Yan, abandoned his post and fled to Jiankang as soon as he heard the Wei had crossed the Huai; the Qi court concentrated its main force at Jiankang and Shitou for a time, and the line south of the Huai was stretched accordingly. At the same time the Wei worked through inducement: in Yiyang a man set himself up as governor of Si, the garrison commander of Jiaocheng surrendered the city, and the governor of Runan with a dragon-general led their men over to the enemy, so that the inside and the outside moved together. When they came to the walls, Wei put its strength against the small city north of the dam at Shouchun, meaning to break the dam and then press on by the eastern road. Yuan Chongzu deliberately left the outer city undefended and instead raised the dam, built the small city and dug a deep ditch around it, arguing that the enemy were greedy and careless and would certainly throw everything at the small city in order to break the dam; and when the assaulting troops had crept up like ants and massed below, he ordered the small dyke opened, the water came down and the Wei camp was drowned. The other side of Qi method was stubborn defence and counterattack: Xuan Yuandu locked his city at Qiushan, the relief under Cui Lingjian bluffed the enemy with torches, Cheng Mai fought to the death at Jiaocheng, and at Zhongli Cui Wenzhong turned a lost action into a victory and sent Cui Xiaobo across the river to pursue. The finest action of the war was Li Anmin's at Huaiyang: he first sent his cousin Changwen with two hundred horsemen as a spearhead who gave ground and fought as they withdrew, drawing several thousand Wei riders into the woods, and then brought his main force out of the ambush to join battle by the Sunxi islet and the bend of the river; the Wei army broke and the dead in the clear water could not be counted. In the second month the General of Partisan Warfare, Huan Kang, beat the Wei again at Huaiyang and took Fanxie city, while Yuan Chongzu crossed the river in counterattack and struck hard at the Wei while they were destroying the Xiacai post. Diplomacy and raids were part of the method as well: an embassy to the Rouran was meant to pin Pingcheng down, and Wei sent Wei Yuan and Xue Huzi to clear the insurgents out of Wugu and cut the Qi network of internal supporters; when the army withdrew, the court ordered Feng Xi to receive the withdrawing generals, and the columns came back in order rather than in a rout.
data: 能站得住的數字有幾條。兵員上，《魏書·高祖紀》記北魏此役分出八名主將：假梁郡王元嘉督二將出淮陰，隴西公拓跋琛三將出廣陵，河東公薛虎子三將出壽春，另有馮熙出義陽、郎大檀出朐城、白吐頭出海西、元泰出連口、封延出角城、賀羅出下蔡，尉元與薛虎子討五固義眾。南齊方面記錄的魏軍總數是「馬步號二十萬」，《南齊書·垣崇祖傳》原話如此，這是南朝一方對敵軍的概估，實數遠少於此，寫作「號」字正說明它是宣稱值；同一時期柔然入寇，《南齊書》作三十萬騎、《資治通鑑》作十餘萬騎，兩說並存，可見南朝估算北方軍力的慣例。壽春小城由數千人守之，《通鑑》作一千人，決堰之後魏軍漂墜塹中，人馬溺死數千人。齊方投入的具體兵力也有數字：蕭惠朗領二千人助蕭景先討義陽，劉伾緒領千人討蠻，李安民遣長文以二百騎為前驅，誘入林中的魏騎達數千之眾。戰線距離上，壽春在建康西北約二百公里，肥水在其城西北流過，淮水在城南不遠。時間上，479年十一月出師，480年正月拓跋琛攻拔馬頭戍、馬頭太守劉從戰死，二月魏軍至壽春而決堰，三月劉昶請退、詔馮熙迎還諸軍，480年七月角城戍主舉城降、九月汝南太守與龍驤將軍率眾內屬，481年正月魏軍至淮陽圍角城、角城軍主成買戰死，二月李安民大破魏軍於清水、同月桓康破敵於淮陽攻陷樊諧城、垣崇祖渡河破魏軍，九月五固義眾被平，自出師至收兵歷時約一年零十個月。制度上的數字屬於戰後：484年魏行俸祿制，戶增調三匹、穀二斛九斗，臧滿一匹者死，485年行均田制，486年行三長制。
dataEn: Only a few figures for this war will bear weight. On strength, the Gao Zu Ji of the Wei Shu records that Northern Wei put eight commanders into the field: the Liang Commandery Prince by Investiture Yuan Jia with two generals through Huaiyin, the Duke of Longxi Tuoba Chen with three through Guangling, the Duke of Hedong Xue Huzi with three through Shouchun, and then Feng Xi through Yiyang, Lang Datan through Qiushan, Bai Tutou through Haixi, Yuan Tai through Liankou, Feng Yan through Jiaocheng and Helao through Xiacai, with Wei Yuan and Xue Huzi sent against the insurgents at Wugu. The total strength of the Wei army recorded on the Qi side is the twenty thousand foot and horse that were claimed, and the Nan Qi Shu biography of Yuan Chongzu has that wording; it is a southern estimate of the enemy, well above the real count, and the verb used is one of announced figure precisely because it was a claim. For the Rouran incursion of the same years the Nan Qi Shu says three hundred thousand horse while the Zizhi Tongjian says a hundred thousand or more; the two figures standing side by side show how the southern court habitually valued northern armies. The small city at Shouchun was held by several thousand men, the Tongjian giving a thousand, and after the dam was cut the Wei were swept into the ditch, men and horses drowning by the thousand. The Qi effort is also given in numbers: Xiao Huilang took two thousand men to help Xiao Jingxian against Yiyang, Liu Pixu took a thousand against the tribes, and Li Anmin sent Changwen ahead with two hundred horsemen, the Wei riders drawn into the woods running to several thousand. On distances, Shouchun lies about two hundred kilometres north-west of Jiankang, the Fei runs past the north-west of the city and the Huai is not far to the south. On time: the army set out in the eleventh month of 479; in the first month of 480 Tuoba Chen took Weitou post and the governor of Weitou, Liu Cong, was killed; in the second month the Wei reached Shouchun and the dam was cut; in the third month Liu Chang asked to withdraw and the court ordered Feng Xi to bring the generals home; in the seventh month of 480 the garrison of Jiaocheng surrendered, and in the ninth the governor of Runan and a dragon-general led their men over to the enemy; in the first month of 481 the Wei reached Huaiyang and surrounded Jiaocheng, where the garrison commander Cheng Mai was killed; in the second month Li Anmin routed the Wei at the clear water, in the same month Huan Kang beat them again at Huaiyang and took Fanxie city and Yuan Chongzu crossed the river and broke them, and in the ninth month the Wugu insurgents were put down, so that the whole business lasted about one year and ten months from the march out to the return. The institutional figures belong to the aftermath: in 484 Wei introduced salaries for officials, adding three bolts of cloth and two hu and nine dou of grain to the household levy, with death the penalty for embezzling as much as one bolt; in 485 came the equal-field system, and in 486 the three-chief system for registering households.
cause: 打起來的起因有三層。最外是名分：北魏打的是劉昶的旗號。劉昶是前劉宋義陽王，465年宗室屠戮中逃奔北魏，魏廷封他丹陽王、屢加厚待，聽到故國滅亡便常涕泣；蕭道成代宋建齊、誅盡劉宋宗室之後，魏廷便以為劉昶恢復宋室為名出兵，藉此把南齊的合法性說成不義之師。第二層是地盤：北魏自太武帝平涼沮渠、得洛陽以來，黃河以南已握在手，但南面隔著淮泗與南齊相望，前一年又取劉宋的青、冀二州與泰山，齊的邊界退到淮水，北魏要打通南北，就必須把淮南與淮北的渡口、戍城一口口吃下。第三層是人心：淮北四州久隸南朝，魏廷屢次遣間諜誘其歸南，齊方也有反覆的接應安排，例如義陽有人自稱司州刺史、角城戍主舉城降、汝南太守與龍驤將軍率眾內屬。齊方也不是全無動作，蕭道成早看出夷虜不識運命、必當動其蟻眾以送劉昶為辭、賊之所衝必在壽春，因此先調垣崇祖鎮壽春、留蕭嶷鎮荊州，又派王洪範出使柔然約期夾擊；只是479年八月柔然十餘萬騎抵平城七百里便獵還，齊軍未及出師，牽制落空。
causeEn: The war began for three layered reasons. The outermost is the matter of legitimacy: Northern Wei fought under the banner of Liu Chang. Liu Chang was the former Prince of Yiyang of the Liu Song, who had fled north during the slaughter of the imperial clan in 465 and whom the Wei court had made Prince of Danyang and treated with repeated kindness, and who was given to tears whenever he heard of the end of his own country; after Xiao Daocheng took the throne from the Song and put the remaining Song clan to the sword, the Wei court marched out in the name of restoring the Song house to Liu Chang, and so presented the new Qi dynasty as an illegitimate usurper. The second layer is territory. Since the Taiwu emperor destroyed the Liang ruler of Guzang and took Luoyang, Wei had held everything south of the Yellow River, yet to the south it still faced Southern Qi across the Huai and the Si, and in the year before it had taken the provinces of Qing and Ji and Mount Tai from the Liu Song, pushing the Qi frontier back to the water; to join north and south Wei had to take the fords and the garrison towns of the Huai basin one at a time. The third layer is the mood of the people. The four provinces north of the Huai had long belonged to the southern court, and Wei repeatedly sent agents to seduce them back south, while Qi had its own repeated arrangements for receiving them: in Yiyang a man set himself up as governor of Si, the garrison of Jiaocheng came over, and the governor of Runan with a dragon-general led their men in. The Qi side was not idle either. Xiao Daocheng had seen early that the barbarians did not understand the turn of fortune and would certainly move their masses to send Liu Chang forward, and that the thrust would come at Shouchun; he therefore moved Yuan Chongzu to hold Shouchun, left Xiao Yi in Jingzhou, and sent Wang Hongfan to the Rouran to arrange a pincer. But in the eighth month of 479 the Rouran horse, more than a hundred thousand strong, came within seven hundred li of Pingcheng and turned back after hunting; the Qi army never marched out, and the intended pincer came to nothing.
impact: 這一役的果實不在土地，而在兩邊的制度走向。軍事上，南齊守住壽春、鍾離、朐山、角城、泗口一線，淮泗防線不失，北魏未能取得淮南，戰線退回淮水，齊廷得以把新朝初立、百廢待興的局面穩住。齊高帝藉戰後整頓：力行節儉，宮禁器物以銅飾者改用鐵，華蓋除金花爪，後宮櫺檻改飾；清查戶籍以增加租役人口；因荊益一帶群蠻屢叛，於480年分荊、益二州置巴州，以三巴校尉明慧昭為巴州刺史、領巴東太守，至齊武帝即位後撤除。北魏這邊的變化更系統化：南征失利後朝野急求改制，484年下詔班俸祿，罷諸商人，戶增調三匹、穀二斛九斗以供官祿，臧滿一匹者死；485年行均田制；486年行三長制整頓戶籍；484年北魏遣李彪回聘南齊，兩國自481年遣使到486年維持約五年無事，487年桓誕反魏奔齊才再啟兵端。對後世而言，494年孝文帝遷都洛陽、495年改姓元氏、499年親征而殂於壺口，都是這幾年平局面積累下來的走向；蕭道成481年崩，蕭賾繼位開永明之治，齊的節儉與整吏則延續了下去。
impactEn: The fruit of this campaign lay not in land but in the direction both states took. Militarily Southern Qi held the line of Shouchun, Zhongli, Qiushan, Jiaocheng and Sikou, the defence of the Huai and the Si was not lost, Northern Wei did not gain the country south of the water, and the front went back to the Huai, which allowed the Qi court to steady a situation that was still settling after the founding of a new dynasty. Xiao Daocheng used the aftermath to reform: he pressed on with frugality, had the copper fittings of palace fittings changed to iron, the golden flower nails removed from the canopies, and the lacquerwork of the inner palace altered; he had the household registers checked in order to enlarge the taxable and liable population; and because the tribes of Jing and Yi rose again and again, in 480 he divided two provinces to create Bazhou, appointing the Inspector of the Three Ba, Ming Huizhao, as governor of Bazhou and administrator of Badong, a post that was later abolished under the next Qi emperor. The change in Northern Wei was more systematic. After the failure of the southern expedition the court pressed on with reform: in 484 an edict established official salaries, dismissed the merchants from the tax privilege, and added three bolts of cloth and two hu and nine dou of grain to each household to pay the officials, with death the penalty for embezzlement of as much as one bolt; in 485 came the equal-field system; in 486 the three-chief system for registering households. In 484 Wei sent Li Biao back as an envoy, and from the Qi embassy of 481 to 486 the two states kept roughly five years of quiet, broken in 487 when Huan Dan rebelled against Wei and fled to Qi. For later history, the move of the capital to Luoyang in 494, the change of surname to Yuan in 495 and the death of Xiaowen on campaign at Hukou in 499 all grew out of the years of peace that followed this war. Xiao Daocheng died in 481, Xiao Ze succeeded him and opened the Yongming prosperity, and the Qi thrift and administrative discipline continued down the line.
result: 結果是南齊全勝、北魏退回。480年三月，魏軍在淮南沒有打開缺口，劉昶以初春降雨將至為由上請退兵，魏廷詔車騎大將軍馮熙督眾迎還假梁郡王嘉等諸軍，撤退有接應掩護，沒有崩潰式潰退，淮北的角城、汝南等新附之地也隨之失去控制。齊軍乘勢追擊：崔文仲在鍾離破敵後派崔孝伯渡淮擊破魏茌眉戍，李安民在淮陽以佯敗誘敵，把數千魏騎引入林地，合戰於孫溪渚，魏軍赴清水死者不可勝數，二月桓康再於淮陽破敵、攻陷樊諧城，垣崇祖趁魏軍摧毀下蔡戍之機渡河北擊大破魏軍。481年正月角城被圍，角城軍主成買戰死，李安民、周盤龍父子進援，孤軍深入的周盤龍與周奉叔在淮陽擊退魏軍；西線因蕭景先嚴守義陽、備好援兵而無功而退。同年九月五固義眾被魏軍平定，齊方在淮北的內應網就此斷絕，桓標之、徐猛子、司馬朗之等數萬人盡歿。齊高帝在同年七月遣車僧朗出使北魏議和，車僧朗在魏廷被降人所刺，魏仍為他送喪，雙方自此通使到486年；487年桓誕策動司雍群蠻起義，才引出494至495年、497至499年的第二、第三次齊魏戰爭。就兵器而言，壽春那一夜的連發弩並沒有單獨贏下任何一仗：它把攻城隊形壓在牆外，贏的是堰、淮水與守方的時間。
resultEn: The result was a complete southern victory and a northern withdrawal. In the third month of 480 the Wei had not opened a gap south of the Huai; Liu Chang asked to withdraw on the ground that the rains of early spring were coming, and the court ordered the General of Chariots and Cavalry Feng Xi to receive the Prince by Investiture Yuan Jia and the other generals and bring them home, so the withdrawal was covered and orderly rather than a collapse, and the newly taken places in the north of the Huai, Jiaocheng and Runan among them, slipped out of Wei control with the army. The Qi pressed the retreat: after Cui Wenzhong beat the Wei at Zhongli he sent Cui Xiaobo across the river and broke the Wei post at Zimei; at Huaiyang Li Anmin gave ground on purpose, drew several thousand Wei riders into the woods, and joined battle at the Sunxi islet, the Wei dead in the clear water past counting; in the second month Huan Kang beat them again at Huaiyang and took Fanxie city, and Yuan Chongzu crossed the river and struck them hard while they were destroying the Xiacai post. In the first month of 481 the Wei reached Huaiyang and surrounded Jiaocheng, where the garrison commander Cheng Mai was killed; Li Anmin and the father and son Zhou Panlong and Zhou Fengshu came up in support, and the two of them, pushing on alone, turned the Wei back at Huaiyang. On the western front, because Xiao Jingxian held Yiyang in strict readiness with reinforcements prepared, the enemy withdrew without effect. In the ninth month of the same year the Wei put down the insurgents at Wugu, the Qi network of contacts in the north of the Huai was cut, and Huan Biao Zhi, Xu Mengzi and Sima Langzhi with tens of thousands of others were destroyed. In the seventh month the Qi emperor sent the Rear Army Colonel Che Senglang as envoy to Wei to open negotiations; Che Senglang was stabbed at the Wei court by one who had come over, and Wei still sent his body home with honours; the two states then kept sending envoys until 486. In 487 Huan Dan stirred the tribes of Si and Yong into revolt, and only then did the second and third of the Qi-Wei wars, of 494 to 495 and 497 to 499, follow. As for the weapon on the card, the repeating crossbow won no single battle by itself on the night at Shouchun: it held the assaulting formation against the foot of the wall, and what won was the dam, the Huai water and the time bought by the defenders.
